name: Admatha
overview: Admatha is a male figure mentioned in Scripture as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. Beyond this distinguished role, no further personal details such as tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded. His position indicates a significant status within the Persian and Median governance structure.
namesAndTitles: The name Admatha is a proper name meaning "unrestrained." This meaning does not appear to be given directly by God but is recorded in the book of Esther (Est 1:14). No additional titles are associated with his name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Admatha beyond his identification as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. There are no listed relatives or connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Admatha's significance lies in his role as one of the seven princes who served under the Persian and Median kings, reflecting the administrative structure of that empire during the period recorded in Esther. His mention highlights the organized governance and the presence of key officials who played roles in the unfolding events of the biblical narrative. Though little else is detailed, his inclusion underscores the historical context of God's providence in preserving His people through earthly authorities.
